newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece sends special forces to Corfu after killing.
newsitem.headline: Greece sends special forces to Corfu after killing.

text.p: Greece will boost its police force on the holiday island of Corfu with 50 specially trained security men after a British tourist was shot dead by a gang raiding his yacht, the public order ministry said on Monday.
The killing has also prompted Britain to warn its citizens on the Ionian island about dangerous boat thieves, apparently from neighbouring Albania.
"Within the next few days 50 men from the special police forces will be sent to Corfu to help guard the borders," a ministry official said.
He said the men, who will wear bullet-proof vests and other special gear, will patrol the whole island and cooperate with the coast guard.
"They will stay as long as it's necessary," he added.
The British travel advisory warns tourists visiting Corfu by boat to stay in harbours where their craft can be guarded and says visitors should avoid marinas from midnight to six a.m.
British tourist Keith Hedley, 57, from Kent was shot dead on Thursday when he tried to stop thieves from stealing a power dinghy tied to his yacht in the early hours of the morning.

Police said armed boat thieves operating by speedboat from the nearby Albanian coast were suspected of killing Hedley. They said the gunmen headed straight for Albania, eight km (4.8 miles) away, after the incident.
The travel advisory said: "This incident, following on from an earlier incident in June when shots were fired at a tourist hotel, comfirms the continuing threat posed by boat thieves."
The Foreign Office issued an earlier warning to British holidaymakers three months ago after boat thieves opened fire with automatic weapons on a coastal holiday resort on Corfu.
Hedley was docked at Gouvia marina, near the main town of Corfu. He was asleep with three friends on the yacht when he heard the thieves and interrupted them, police said.
Ministry officials said Greece was working with Interpol to try to stop the sale in Albania of about 100 boats which are thought to be stolen from Greek harbours, mainly in Corfu.
They said Interpol officials were already in Albania, cooperating with local authorities, to try to deter the sale.
